items.iso-42001::clause-4: Identify the internal and external matters that shape the AI management system and affect what it is meant to achieve.
items.iso-42001::clause-5: Senior leadership must own the AI management system — set and communicate the AI policy and assign who is responsible and accountable.
items.iso-42001::clause-6: Before planning changes to the AIS, weigh the context issues (4.1) and interested-party requirements (4.2), decide which risks and opportunities to act on, fold AI risk into the firm's overall risk process, and set measurable AI objectives.
items.iso-42001::clause-7: Provide the resources the AI management system needs — including managing data quality, competence, awareness and communication.
items.iso-42001::clause-8: Plan, run and control the processes the AI system lifecycle needs, including deliberately introducing new AI systems, and keep the records the system requires.
items.iso-42001::clause-9: Check how the AI systems and the management system itself are performing — with planned internal audits and top-management review.
items.iso-42001::clause-10: Keep making the AI management system better suited, adequate and effective — correcting failures to conform and acting on them.
